title: Charging System Warning Light
summary: Practical diagnostic path for battery light, low voltage, and charging-system complaints.
intro: Charging warnings should be checked as a system: battery health, alternator output, belt drive, fuses, and grounds can all create the same customer complaint.
common_sounds: Dimming lights or weak blower speed
quick_checks: Load test the battery before judging alternator output
Check charging voltage with electrical loads on
Inspect belt condition, tension, and pulley alignment
Check alternator output cable, main fuse, and engine grounds
common_causes: High resistance in charge cable, fuse, or ground path
diagnostic_paths: If battery fails load testing, correct battery condition before final alternator judgment.
If charging voltage is low with a known-good battery, inspect alternator output and belt drive.
If voltage is intermittent, inspect connector fit, charge cable, main fuse, and grounds.

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Battery and Alternator Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Separate battery capacity from alternator output before quoting either part.
checks: Measure charging voltage with loads on
Check battery light behavior after start-up

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Belt and Cable Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Charging output can fail from belt slip, poor grounds, or high resistance in the output cable.
checks: Inspect serpentine belt and tensioner condition
Voltage-drop charge cable and ground paths
Check main charging fuse or fusible link

recommended_repairs.description: Use when charging output, belt drive, and wiring checks prove alternator failure.

recommended_repairs.title: Battery Blueprint
